Ondansetron has been successfully used by continuous subcutaneous infusion to control intractable nausea and vomiting.1 Despite concern about the low pH of ondansetron injection there was no problem with the skin at the infusion site. An oral protocol for chemotherapy-induced emesis in children has been described;2 efficacy was similar to intravenous use. 1. Mulvenna PM, Regnard CFB. Subcutaneous ondansetron. Administration in hepatic impairment. Licensed drug in- formation recommends that the dose of ondansetron should not exceed 8 mg daily in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment.
